name: University of California. Los Angeles - Extension
overview:
The University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is a public land-grant research university in Los Angeles, California. UCLA’s academic roots were established in 1882 as a teachers college then known as the southern branch of the California State Normal School (now San José State University). This school was absorbed with the official founding of UCLA as the Southern Branch of the University of California in 1919, making it the second-oldest of the 10-campus University of California system (after UC Berkeley).

UCLA is considered one of the United States’ Public Ivies, and is frequently ranked among the best universities in the world by major college and university rankings

UCLA student-athletes compete as the Bruins in the Pac-12 Conference. The Bruins have won 119 NCAA team championships, second only to Stanford University's 128 team titles. In total, 410 Bruins have made Olympic teams, winning 270 Olympic medals: 136 gold, 71 silver, and 63 bronze. UCLA has been represented in every Olympics since the university's founding with one exception (1924) and has had a gold medalist in every Olympics the U.S. participated in since 1932.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


In the past the partner has asked for the following:

  • Photocopy of passport / Residence permit (valid more than 6 months after return)
  • Registration forms for UCSB (provided once the destination has been validated by the jury)
  • A letter from the bank with a provision of $20,000 dated less than 6 months
  • If the bank letter is from a parent's bank account, it must attest to the relationship and mention that the amount available may be used for your expenses during your year abroad in the United States.
  • Course selection form for UCLA (provided once the destination has been validated by the jury)
  • University insurance subscription consent form (provided once the destination has been validated by the jury)

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


2. Visa

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website.


1/ Admission letter and I-20 form

When you have been admitted to the university, you will receive an acceptance letter and an I-20 form, allowing you to apply for the F-1 student visa at the embassy. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2/ Pay the SEVIS fees

You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3/Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4/Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.

You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment for submitting a file, here.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3. Insurance and Health

UCLA requires students to purchase the university health insurance, unless your health insurance meets the criteria for a waiver.

More information, including rates, policy details, and criteria for exemptions can be found on this website.

You must demonstrate proof of health insurance coverage before arriving to the U.S., as part of your I-20 application.

In order to be fully covered in the event of an accident (especially outside the region), we recommend that all students take out international insurance during their Tech 4 abroad. It is imperative that you take out an international insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. 


To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information. 


For more information, you can consult the country's health file a: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/etats-unis.

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside of France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html

Off-campus, non-UCLA housing is available year-round; students make reservations directly with housing providers.

International students typically live off campus, usually in privately owned residence halls, homestays, or furnished apartments. See the link above for more information.


UCLA on-campus housing is available in summer only.
courses:
Credits

Students must take a total of 36 local credits per semester to obtain 60 ECTS for the year, not counting EIP credits.

Most courses are 4 credits, and UCLA functions on a trimester system, so this means 3 courses per trimester.


Epitech will cover the tuition fees at UCLA Extension to the extent of the credits required according to the program followed. Any additional module you wish to take will be at your expense.


Academic Calendar (more information here)

  • Fall Quarter: September – December
  • Winter Quarter: January – March
  • Spring Quarter: March – June


Department and Courses

Students will complete a dual certificate in Data Analytics and Cybersecurity.

Students will be enrolled in the program Data Science with Concentration in Cybersecurity (see details here), for a total of 32 credits (8 classes). The remaining class (4 credits) can be chosen from any course in the Machine Learning course listed below.


Course Format and Workload

As the curriculum at UCLA Extension is more theoretical than that at Epitech, you should expect:

  • have homework to do
  • current presence is required
  • theoretical teaching
  • lecture

The grading system is based on a scale from 1 to 100. In order to pass a class, you must receive at least 70.


Important Notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.

Financial Overview (4th Year EPITECH)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees. Epitech will pay the tuition fees at UCLA to the extent of the credits required according to the program followed. Any additional module will be at your expense.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses / Estimated Budget

The local currency is the Dollar. 1 € = 1.16USD (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

  • Books & supplies: 1600$
  • Internet: 50$ / month (45 euros)

  • Housing and Food: 20 000$/9 months
  • Transportation: 1 600$/9 months

You can get a general idea of how much you will need for 9 months in Los Angeles with this website, using the off-campus column (do not take into account tuition as Epitech pays this on your behalf).
